skill.name: plan-harder
skill.description: Create detailed, phased implementation plans for engineering tasks, features, and bugs.
skill.summary: Turn a request into a researched, testable implementation plan.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: All four static findings were false positives caused by Markdown inline code or fenced template text in SKILL.md. No executable commands, prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or other semantic security concerns were found during context review.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 71 uses Markdown inline code to describe a filename suffix, not shell or Ruby execution. There is no executable command or user-controlled command construction.
Line 74 shows a Markdown filename example inside backticks. It is documentation text and does not invoke an external command.
Line 75 shows another Markdown filename example inside backticks. No command execution syntax is present outside documentation formatting.
Line 92 starts a fenced Markdown plan template, and the block contains document structure only. It is not executable shell, Ruby, or script content.

content.value_statement: Complex code changes fail when requirements, risks, and validation are vague. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce phased implementation plans.
actual_capabilities: Researches codebase structure, patterns, dependencies, and related components before planning.
Breaks requests into phased sprints with demoable and testable increments.
Defines atomic tasks with dependencies, acceptance criteria, and validation steps.
Creates a saved Markdown plan file with a task-based filename.
Reviews the plan for risks, missing steps, and ambiguous requirements.
limitations: Only activates when the user specifically asks to plan harder.
Creates plans only and instructs the agent not to implement the work.
May need user answers when scope, priorities, or constraints are unclear.
Plan quality depends on accessible project files and available context.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Build
use_cases.description: Convert a feature request into sprints, tasks, dependencies, and validation checks before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Investigate likely causes, affected files, edge cases, and rollback needs for a risky bug fix.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Team Work
use_cases.description: Create a plan with parallelizable tasks and clear acceptance criteria for several contributors.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Plan Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need a structured plan for a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan harder for adding a user profile edit page. Research the codebase and save a phased implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Bug Fix Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a defect needs investigation before code changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan harder for fixing the checkout validation bug. Include likely causes, affected files, tests, risks, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-System Feature Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a feature spans backend, frontend, data, and deployment work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan harder for implementing organization-level billing. Include sprints, dependencies, migration concerns, security checks, and demo criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Team Execution Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when work must be divided across contributors with clear sequencing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan harder for replacing the search provider. Identify parallel tasks, ownership boundaries, validation gates, launch steps, and fallback options.

output_examples.input: Plan harder for adding Google sign-in.
output_examples.output: A saved Markdown plan with research notes, phased sprints, OAuth setup tasks, callback routing, UI work, tests, risks, and rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: Plan harder for fixing slow dashboard loading.
output_examples.output: A saved plan that separates profiling, query review, caching options, UI loading states, performance validation, and production monitoring.

output_examples.input: Plan harder for migrating the notifications system.
output_examples.output: A phased plan covering current behavior, data migration, compatibility work, rollout checks, failure modes, and post-launch verification.

best_practices: Provide the goal, known constraints, target users, and deadline before invoking the skill.
Answer clarification questions with concrete scope decisions and priority order.
Review the saved plan before implementation and confirm validation expectations.
anti_patterns: Do not use it when you want immediate implementation instead of planning.
Do not leave major product decisions unresolved and expect a final plan.
Do not treat the generated plan as proof that code changes are safe.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a saved Markdown implementation plan with research, sprints, tasks, validation, risks, and rollback guidance.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly tells the agent to create the plan and not implement it.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before complex features, risky bug fixes, migrations, or work that needs clear task sequencing.

faq.question: Does it ask questions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can ask targeted questions when scope, constraints, priorities, or edge cases are unclear.

faq.question: Can it help with team coordination?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for atomic tasks, dependencies, and validation steps that help split work across contributors.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
